privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This Privacy Policy explains how enpii studio (“we”) collects, uses, and protects information when you use EnStorage (the “Service”). EnStorage is a self-hosted application: all data is processed on an instance you control, and your files are stored directly in your own Google Drive account. By using the Service, you agree to the practices described below.
privacy.dataWeCollectBody:
Basic Google profile: When you sign in or connect an account with Google, we receive your name and email address (scopes `userinfo.profile` and `userinfo.email`). We use these only to identify your account; your profile picture is neither stored nor displayed by the application.

OAuth tokens: For each Google Drive account you connect, we store an access token, a refresh token, and its expiry. Refresh tokens are encrypted with AES-256 at rest before being written to the database. We never receive or see your Google password.

File metadata: We store the metadata required to manage files (name, size, MIME type, folder path, upload date, star flags, share link token and settings, and the object ID in Google Drive). The file itself lives in your Google Drive account, not on our server.

API keys & webhooks: When you create a personal access token, only a bcrypt hash and the 8-character prefix are stored. The plaintext token is shown once and cannot be retrieved again. For webhooks we store the label, target URL, event list, and an encrypted secret.

Usage data: We log basic request metadata (timestamp, endpoint, status code, API key ID) for security, auditing of sensitive actions, and abuse prevention. We do not ship third-party analytics, advertising, or tracking pixels.
privacy.howWeUseBody:
We use the information collected solely to operate the Service as you request: authenticating you, routing file writes to the Google Drive account with the largest remaining quota, storing and retrieving your files, generating the share links you ask for, showing combined quota totals, and notifying you of account activity through webhooks.

We do not sell, rent, trade, or relinquish your personal information to third parties. We do not use your Google Drive data — including its content, names, or any metadata — for unrelated tracking, targeted advertising, or training general-purpose artificial intelligence / machine learning models.
privacy.googleScopes: 3. Google Drive API Policy & OAuth2 Scopes
privacy.googleScopesBody:
EnStorage connects to Google Drive on your behalf, so it must comply with the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.

The scopes requested on the Google consent screen are:

- `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive` — read, create, update, and delete the files and folders EnStorage manages, and read account quota information (`about.get`), which is what lets smart routing pick the account with the most free space.
- `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.profile` and `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email` — the basic profile used for sign-in and to display the account email address.

Google shows these scopes explicitly on the consent screen before any token is issued, and consent is granted by you, not by us. EnStorage uses the permission only for the file-management operations you ask for: files are written inside an `EnStorage` folder on your Drive, and no other Google service is accessed.

You can revoke the permission at any time, either from the EnStorage dashboard or from your Google account permissions page. Reading global quota and scanning an existing folder structure genuinely requires the `drive` scope, so we present that accurately rather than claiming narrower access than the product really uses.
privacy.limitedUseBody:
In line with the Limited Use principles of the Google API Services User Data Policy, we state that:

- We only use or share user data accessed from Google APIs to provide or allow access to legitimate EnStorage features that are relevant to you.
- We never sell Google Drive user data in any way.
- We never use or share that data for advertising, regardless of its source.
- We never use or allow the use of that data to train machine learning or AI models, including generative AI models, either directly or as part of another project or product.
- We restrict access to that data only to personnel who need it to process it on our behalf, and ensure they are bound by confidentiality obligations.

Self-hosted instances run on your own infrastructure, so the data controller for your Google Drive data is you, not enpii studio.
privacy.sharingBody:
Files or folders you choose to share can be accessed by anyone holding the share link. Links contain a random token and can be given an expiry date and a maximum view count. Links can be revoked at any time from the Folder or File page, or through the REST API (`DELETE /api/v1/files/{id}/share`).

When a folder is shared, its files are rendered through the EnStorage proxy so your private Google Drive links are never exposed to the recipient. You remain responsible for the content you share through those links.
privacy.thirdPartyBody:
We rely on the following third parties to operate the Service:

Google (OAuth2 & Google Drive API): processing is subject to the Google Privacy Policy. We only request the scopes needed to handle sign-in and the file management you ask for, in accordance with the Limited Use clause above.

Hosting infrastructure: on self-hosted instances all data resides on servers you control. On managed deployments, data may transit the infrastructure used to run the Service.

Email providers: if your instance sends transactional email (for example notifications or password resets), mail is routed through the SMTP configuration you provide.
privacy.securityBody:
We apply industry-standard measures to protect your data:

- Transport: all web and REST API communication is served over HTTPS/TLS.
- OAuth tokens: access and refresh tokens are encrypted with Laravel Crypt (AES-256-CBC) before being written to your instance database, keyed by APP_KEY.
- API keys: stored as a bcrypt hash plus a plaintext prefix for lookup; the secret value can never be read back.
- Account passwords: hashed one-way, never stored in plaintext.
- Isolation: files, folders, and Drive credentials are scoped per user so other users cannot read them.
- Per-key rate limiting and audit logs for sensitive actions.

Full details of the security architecture are on the Security & Google API Disclosure page. No system is completely secure; if you discover a vulnerability, follow the reporting procedure described on that page.
privacy.retentionBody:
Your files remain in your Google Drive account until you delete them. Deleting a file or folder moves it to a soft-deleted state and it is permanently removed after 30 days unless you restore it.

Specific deletions:

- Detaching a Google account: when you revoke a Google account from EnStorage, we attempt to revoke the token at Google, then permanently delete the refresh token, access token, and all file metadata associated with that account from the database.
- Deleting your EnStorage account: all of your rows (files, folders, share links, API keys, webhooks, activity logs, and Google tokens) are permanently deleted through cascade relations, and tokens are revoked at Google. Files that remain in your Drive are still yours and you can manage them directly in Drive.
- Share links: revocation takes effect immediately; expired tokens are revoked automatically by a scheduler.

Once access is revoked, EnStorage has no way to read the contents of your Drive anymore.
privacy.yourRightsBody:
You hold full control over access to your data:

- Revoking access: remove the Google account from the Google Accounts page in EnStorage, or open Google Account Settings → Security → Third-party apps & services (myaccount.google.com/permissions) and revoke EnStorage. Revoking on Google's side also severs the connection permanently.
- Deleting data: delete files, folders, or share links at any time; delete your account from the Profile page to erase all local metadata.
- Portability: every operation is available through the REST API, so you can export your file listing and contents programmatically.
- Access & correction: review or change your profile, language, and password from the Profile page.

If you are in the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, or California, you have additional rights under applicable law (GDPR / CCPA), including the right to data portability and the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority. On self-hosted deployments you exercise these requests through your instance administrator.
privacy.changesBody: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. Material changes will be announced through the Service and on this page together with the “Last updated” date. Continued use of the Service after changes indicates acceptance of the updated policy.
privacy.contactBody: For privacy questions, questions about Google API Services User Data Policy compliance, or to exercise your rights, contact us at enpiiofficial@gmail.com. For security issues, use the vulnerability reporting channel on the Security page.
privacy.summary: EnStorage is non-custodial: your files are stored directly in your own Google Drive, never on our servers. We keep only OAuth tokens (encrypted with AES-256-CBC using your instance APP_KEY) and file metadata in a database you control. Google data is never sold, never shared for advertising, and never used to train AI models.

security.title: Security & Google API Disclosure
security.intro: This page describes EnStorage's security architecture and our formal disclosure regarding use of the Google Drive API. It applies to every client: the web pages and the REST API. The guiding principle is simple — EnStorage is never the storage. Your files stay in your Google Drive account while our system manages only tokens, routing, and metadata on the instance you control.
security.architectureBody:
When you upload a file, the backend receives the byte stream from your client, holds it briefly in a temporary directory on the instance, then forwards it to the destination Google Drive account inside the `EnStorage` folder using a resumable upload. Once the write to Drive completes and an image thumbnail has been generated, that temporary copy is deleted. The instance does not use its disk as permanent storage and keeps no warehouse of copies.

What follows from that:

- No third-party server holds the contents of your files; the only place they live is your own Google Drive.
- A file is uploaded whole to a single destination account — never split or spread across accounts.
- Revoking access immediately removes the system's ability to read your Drive.
- Disconnecting an account or deleting the instance leaves no hidden copy with us, because we never had one.
security.transportBody: Every data path runs over HTTPS/TLS: web pages, OAuth callbacks, the stream/preview proxy, and all REST API endpoints. We recommend serving public deployments behind a reverse proxy with valid certificates, HSTS, and regularly updated TLS suites. Security headers are sent on web responses, and shared content is rendered through the proxy so your Google Drive object IDs are never leaked to end clients.
security.atRest: 3. Encryption at Rest for OAuth Tokens
security.atRestBody:
Google access and refresh tokens are stored encrypted with AES-256 at rest in the local database (`AES-256-CBC` cipher), with the encryption key derived from your instance's `APP_KEY`, which is never stored alongside the database.

Operational consequences you should understand:

- If the `APP_KEY` is lost, stored tokens cannot be recovered and every Google account must be reconnected.
- Because that key is yours, we are cryptographically unable to open your tokens.
- We recommend volume encryption on the database host, encrypted backups, and planned `APP_KEY` rotation in line with your organization's security policy.
security.credentialsBody:
Account passwords are one-way hashed with bcrypt and are never stored or transmitted in plaintext. API keys are generated in the format `en_<8-char-prefix>_<40-char-secret>`; only the bcrypt hash and the prefix are stored in the database, while the secret value is displayed once at creation and cannot be retrieved afterwards. Inbound requests are verified by matching the prefix and then comparing the hash (bcrypt compare).

In addition: every request is logged with its key ID, scopes are enforced per endpoint (`read`, `write`, `delete`, `full`), keys can expire or be revoked at any time, and rate limiting thwarts brute-force attempts. We recommend one key per integration with the minimum scope, plus periodic rotation.
security.scopesBody:
EnStorage requests only the Google scopes it genuinely needs, and never silently: `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive` for file management and the quota read (`about.get`) that smart routing depends on, plus `userinfo.profile` and `userinfo.email` for the basic sign-in profile. The Google consent screen lists the requested scopes explicitly before any token is issued, and consent is granted by you, not by us.

Refresh tokens are used only to reissue access tokens for operations on your account's behalf; we never sell, share, or publish Google credentials to third parties. The app is designed to meet the verification requirements and the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.

Straight note: the `drive` scope covers your whole Drive, not only the EnStorage folder. We chose it because combined quota across accounts cannot be read with a narrower scope. For that reason, revocation should be done through Google's own permissions page, and an instance is best run with the Drive accounts you deliberately dedicate to EnStorage.
security.limitedUseBody:
We comply with the Limited Use requirements of the Google API Services User Data Policy. We explicitly state that Google Drive user data:

- Is never sold or rented to anyone.
- Is never used for advertising or unrelated tracking beyond the features you request.
- Is never used to train general-purpose machine learning or artificial intelligence models, by us or by anyone acting on our behalf.
- Is never shared with third parties except for processing on our behalf under confidentiality obligations, or where lawfully required.
- Is only accessed as strictly necessary to perform the file-management functions you instruct.
security.isolationBody: Every database row — files, folders, Google accounts, API keys, share links, and activity logs — is scoped to its owner's `user_id` and verified on each request. User A's Google accounts cannot be seen, referenced, or used to store User B's files. `owner` and `member` roles differ only in governance actions (user invitations and system-wide audit logs) and never grant access to another user's Drive credentials. API key and Google account management endpoints accept user sessions only and reject API key authentication.
security.sharingBody: Share links use unguessable random tokens, can be given an expiry date and a maximum view count, and can be revoked instantly from the UI or the API. Shared files and folders are rendered through a proxy so the original Google Drive URL is never exposed. Links that expire or reach their view limit are revoked automatically by a scheduler. We recommend always setting an expiry and a view limit when sharing sensitive content.
security.loggingBody: The instance records request metadata (timestamp, endpoint, status code, key/session identity) and audit logs for sensitive actions such as API key creation/revocation, Google account connection/revocation, share link changes, and delete operations. These logs serve security and forensic needs, not behavioral profiling. No third-party analytics, advertising, or tracking pixels ship in the codebase. Because the instance is yours, log retention and access are under your administrator's control.
security.userControlsBody:
You can revoke access at any time through two independent paths:

- From EnStorage: open the Google Accounts page and choose Revoke. The system revokes the token at Google (best effort) and permanently deletes the refresh token, access token, and related metadata from the database.
- From Google: open myaccount.google.com/permissions, select EnStorage, and revoke access. You can also review and sign out of sessions via myaccount.google.com/signin.

After revocation the tokens are worthless and the system can no longer read or write files in your Drive. Deleting your EnStorage account from the Profile page performs a thorough deletion of all your local metadata plus token revocation at Google.
security.deletion: 11. Data Deletion & Right to Be Forgotten
security.deletionBody: Deletion is permanent and layered: disconnecting a Google account revokes its token at Google and removes that token plus the account's metadata; deleting an EnStorage account removes files, folders, share links, API keys, webhooks, and logs through cascade relations; shutting down an instance removes all metadata from your system. Deleting a file in EnStorage also calls the Google Drive API to remove the object, so the file disappears from your Drive rather than merely from a listing. Files already deleted on the Drive side are reconciled in the metadata by the cleanup scheduler. Because file contents are never kept permanently on our server, no additional deletion request to enpii studio is needed.
security.userResponsibilitiesBody:
Because EnStorage is self-hosted, the security of your deployment is also your responsibility. We recommend:

- Keeping `APP_KEY` in a secret manager, never in the database or a repository.
- Restricting database access and accepting connections only from the application network.
- Serving the instance behind a reverse proxy with current TLS, HSTS, and rate limiting.
- Applying security updates regularly and keeping encrypted database backups.
- Enabling two-step verification on connected Google accounts and creating minimum-scope API keys.
- Removing unused accounts, revoking unused API keys, and reviewing activity logs periodically.
security.vulnerabilityBody:
If you find a vulnerability in EnStorage, please report it responsibly to enpiiofficial@gmail.com with the subject “Security”. Do not publish vulnerability details (public issues, social media, or blog posts) before it is addressed.

Upon receiving a report we will acknowledge it within at most 7 days, assess impact and severity, prepare a fix or mitigation for the next release, and coordinate a disclosure timeline with you if you would like credit. Please avoid accessing other users' production data, disrupting the service, or downloading data as evidence — demonstrating the vulnerable point is enough.
security.statusBody: No system is completely secure. Encryption protects tokens and transport, but it does not eliminate risks such as compromised Google credentials, misconfigured instances, or social engineering. We update this page as security practices evolve; material changes are announced through releases along with the “Last updated” date on this page. For the privacy aspects of your personal data see the Privacy Policy; for usage conditions see the Terms of Service.
security.summary: Files stream straight into your Google Drive without ever landing on server disk. Refresh tokens are sealed with AES-256-CBC through Laravel Crypt using a local APP_KEY, transport runs over TLS, and every grant can be revoked instantly — no AI training, no data resale.

features.title: What you will actually use every day
features.subtitle: EnStorage solves a simple problem: too many Drive accounts, too little space in each of them.

aggregation.title: One place for every account
aggregation.body: Connect your Google Drive accounts and they all show up in one panel — quota, email address, and connection status in a single list.

routing.title: Automatic smart routing
routing.body: Every new file goes straight to the account with the largest free space that can fit it. You never have to pick a destination.

viewer.title: Open and play in place
viewer.body: View documents and images, or play video, without downloading first. Everything runs through the EnStorage proxy, so your Drive links stay hidden from other people.

isolation.title: Your data belongs to you alone
isolation.body: Files, folders, and credentials are strictly separated between users. One person's Google account cannot be opened by another user on the same instance.

api.title: REST API and API keys
api.body: Connect storage to your scripts, backend, or n8n workflows. Create an API key with separate scopes, then use it exactly like the examples in the Developer section below.

security.title: Built for an instance you control
security.subtitle: Every point below is real system behaviour you can verify on your own installation.

nonCustodial.title: Files never land on our server
nonCustodial.body: Files are forwarded to the destination Google Drive account, then the temporary copy on the server is deleted. EnStorage stores metadata and tokens, not the contents of your files.

token.title: Encrypted OAuth tokens
token.body: Access and refresh tokens are encrypted with Laravel Crypt (AES-256-CBC) using the APP_KEY in your instance. Without that APP_KEY, the database contents cannot be read.

limitedUse.title: Google Limited Use compliant
limitedUse.body: Your Google Drive data is never sold, never shared with advertisers, and never used to train AI models. You can revoke the permission at any time.

keys.delete: Delete files, folders, and connected Google accounts.
keys.full: Combines every scope above into a single key.

footer.tagline: A self-hosted multi-account Google Drive aggregator. Never Leaves Your Drive.
footer.copyright: Copyright {{year}} enpii studio. All rights reserved.
footer.selfHostedNote: EnStorage runs on an instance you own.

teaser.title: The full API reference lives on its own page
teaser.subtitle: This is the short version: one base URL, one authorization header, and four steps to your first upload. The endpoint tables, status codes, and copyable cURL examples live in the documentation portal.

docs.title: REST API documentation
docs.subtitle: One base URL, one authorization header. Every example on this page can be copied and run against your EnStorage instance as-is. A short summary of each endpoint lives in the tables near the bottom.

start.title: Four steps to your first upload
start.subtitle: Prepare a key, send a file, read the pooled quota, then share the result. Every step hits the same endpoints the web dashboard uses.

prepare.title: Prepare an API key
prepare.body: Create the key on the **API Key** page in the dashboard. The secret is shown only once, at creation time.

upload.title: Upload a file
upload.body: Send one or several files at once. A `202 Accepted` response means the file entered the queue; the write to Google Drive happens asynchronously.

summary.title: Read the pooled quota
summary.body: `GET /storage/summary` totals the quota of every active account and includes a per-account breakdown.

search.title: Search files
search.body: Search is `typo-tolerant` and can sweep an entire folder subtree with `recursive=1`.

share.title: Share a file
share.body: Create a public link with `expires_at` and `max_views`. The link can be revoked at any time.

auth.title: Two access modes
auth.subtitle: The web dashboard uses Sanctum cookies, while machine integrations use an API key. Scopes only apply to API-key requests.
auth.apiKeyNote: Paste the key into the `Authorization` header with a `Bearer` prefix. This is the default mode for scripts and backend services.
auth.headerNote: The dedicated `X-API-Key` header helps when the `Authorization` value is already taken by another system.
auth.sanctumNote: Web logins store the token in an `httpOnly` cookie. The cookie travels automatically, so there is no header to manage.
auth.keyFormatBody: Keys follow the `en_<8-char-prefix>_<40-char-secret>` pattern. The prefix exists for fast lookups; the secret is never stored in plaintext.
auth.sanctumOnlyWarning: `/api-keys/*` and `/webhooks/*` are reachable through Sanctum only, never through an API key.

scopes.title: API key scopes
scopes.subtitle: A single key can hold several scopes. Requests are rejected with `403` when the scope is missing.

allows.read: Every `GET` endpoint: files, folders, accounts, and quota summaries.
allows.full: Everything above. A convenient shortcut for a single all-purpose key of your own.
allows.sanctum: Reserved for login sessions (Sanctum cookies). Cannot be granted to an API key.
allows.public: No credentials at all, for example share links and sign-in pages.

envelope.title: Response format
envelope.subtitle: Every JSON response uses the same envelope so clients can parse it uniformly.
envelope.note: Validation errors (`422`) automatically adopt this envelope, with the per-field map inside `data`.

errors.title: Status codes
errors.subtitle: The codes below appear on responses wrapped in `success: false`.
errors.ok: The request finished and the payload lives in `data`.
errors.created: A new resource was created, such as an account or folder.
errors.accepted: The request was queued; poll `files/{id}/status` for the final result.
errors.unauthenticated: The token is missing, expired, or invalid.
errors.forbidden: Insufficient scope, or the resource belongs to another user.
errors.notFound: The path, id, or token does not exist.
errors.conflict: State conflict, such as a duplicate name or an unfinished file.
errors.validation: The request body failed validation; field details are in `data`.
errors.rateLimited: Request limit exceeded; wait for the `Retry-After` header.
errors.upstream: The Google API refused or returned an error.
errors.unconfigured: The instance is not configured yet, for example empty OAuth credentials.

rateLimit.title: Request limits
rateLimit.subtitle: Throttling is enforced per key on the server.
rateLimit.pageSubtitle: Three throttle layers run at once; the strictest one decides the outcome.

limits.sanctum: Follows the default Laravel throttle for login sessions.
limits.auth: A separate throttle, for example `5` sign-in attempts per minute.

rateLimit.retryNote: When a limit is hit the server answers `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header in seconds.

shareLinks.title: Share links
shareLinks.subtitle: One file or folder can hold several active links at the same time.
shareLinks.public: Unrestricted: anyone holding the link can open it, no login required.
shareLinks.views: View cap: `max_views` stops the link once reached.

notes.cookieNote: The same response also sets an `httpOnly` cookie for the web dashboard.
notes.sanctumOnlyNote: `/api-keys/*` and `/webhooks/*` are reachable through a Sanctum session only, never through an API key.
notes.keyFormatNote: Keys follow `en_<8-char-prefix>_<40-char-secret>`: the prefix speeds up lookups, the secret is never stored in plaintext.
notes.asyncNote: `202` means the file entered the queue. Poll `GET /files/{id}/status` until it reads `done`.
notes.rootDefaultNote: Without `folder_id` the result is scoped to the root. Send `folder_id=` (empty) for files in every folder.
notes.noTempStorageNote: Bytes are proxied straight from Drive to the client; your server keeps no copy.
notes.statusValuesNote: Status moves `pending` → `uploading` → `done`, or `failed` when Drive refuses.
notes.rangeNote: The proxy streams the response, so HTML5 players can seek without exposing a Drive link.
notes.renameOnMoveNote: If the name is taken in the destination folder, EnStorage appends a suffix (`laporan (1).pdf`) and reports it in `renamed`.
notes.permanentNote: There is no EnStorage trash bin: once gone, the object is gone from Google Drive too.
notes.batchStarNote: Batch move and batch star run as repeated `PATCH /files/{id}` calls; only batch delete has its own route.
notes.publicUrlNote: The URL must be public: private hosts, non-80/443 ports, and suspicious redirects are rejected.
notes.resumeNote: Re-sending a chunk you already delivered is safe — the server answers `200` without duplicating bytes.
notes.cycleNote: Moving a folder inside one of its own descendants is rejected with `422`.
notes.quotaCacheNote: Quota is read from the Google API and cached for 5 minutes per account, so this call is cheap.
notes.oauthOutNote: Raw Google OAuth callbacks are deliberately undocumented: connect accounts through the dashboard instead.
notes.shareIdempotentNote: A second call returns the same token; use `/share-links` when you need extra links.
notes.revokeAllNote: `DELETE /files/{id}/share` revokes every link on the file at once.
notes.streamNote: Without `?info=1` the response is binary, so the same URL feeds a `<video>` / `<audio>` element.
notes.starredNote: Stars live in the EnStorage index, not as a Google Drive property.
notes.cursorNote: Pass `next_cursor` back unchanged; the format is opaque and can change.
notes.webhookSanctumNote: Like API keys: session auth only.
notes.signatureNote: Verify the `X-Webhook-Signature` header with that secret before trusting a payload.

p.bearerHeader: Your `en_…` API key or Sanctum token, prefixed with `Bearer `.
p.keyExpires: Auto-expiry; leave empty for a permanent key.
p.keyId: Key id as shown in the list.
p.fileField: Send one file with `file=@…` or several with `file[]=@…`. Up to 10 files, 1 GB each.
p.folderIdField: Destination folder; omit for the root.
p.clientKey: Your own id for matching the reply. `A-Za-z0-9._:-`, up to 128 characters.
p.shareable: Create a public link as soon as the upload is accepted.
p.shareExpiresField: Expiry for the link created with this upload.
p.contentHash: SHA-256 hex (64 characters) for client-side dedup.
p.folderIdQuery: `null` or empty means the root; send `folder_id=` empty for every folder.
p.searchQuery: Substring match on the name, case-insensitive.
p.statusQuery: `pending`, `uploading`, `done`, `failed`. Failed uploads are hidden by default.
p.fileId: File id from a listing or an upload reply.
p.inlineTrue: `1` so the browser plays instead of saving.
p.folderIdBody: Destination folder; `null` moves to the root.
p.idsBatch: 1–50 ids. Ones you do not own come back in `not_found`.
p.sourceUrl: Public http/https URL the server can fetch.
p.nameOverride: Override the stored name; defaults to the URL or Content-Disposition.
p.fileName: Final file name, up to 255 characters.
p.parentId: New parent; `null` moves to the root.
p.deleteFiles: `1` also deletes the files inside from Drive.
p.shareExpires: When the link stops working; empty for never.
p.shareId: Link row id, not the token.
p.shareToken: 32 hex characters from the share URL.
p.infoQuery: `1` returns metadata JSON instead of bytes.
p.fileIdInFolder: For shared folders: pick one file inside.
p.hashesQuery: Comma-separated SHA-256 hex list, up to 100.
p.webhookActive: Pause watching without deleting the configuration.
